full_judgment: 5. On the other hand Mr. Md. Nurul Amin appearing with Mr. Fazlul Haque Chowdhury, the learned Advocates for the opposite party No. 1 submit that the trial court upon considering all material evidences on record and being satisfied with the same passed the decree. The defendants having failed to file any written statement in 16 years denying the allegations of the plaint actually proves that there is no case against the plaintiff. Moreover, the defendant No. 21 entered appearance in the suit on 25.5.1999 but neither he filed written statement nor he finally contested the same and having not cross examined the P.W., the evidence of P.W. remains uncontroverted and there being nothing contrary in record, the evidence and the documents filed by the plaintiff are found to have been proved. The learned Assistant Judge having taken notice of all such evidences on record and having considered the same observed that upon considering the plaint, the evidences both oral and documentary produced by the plaintiff, the case of the plaintiff is found to have been proven and as such the ex-parte decree has rightly been passed. He next submits that the learned judgment of the court of appeal below having affirmed the judgment of the trial court does not require to strictly follow the provision of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code. Moreover , Rule 143 of the C.R.O. provides that "Judgment in ex-parte case shall state specifically and explicitly which of the reliefs are granted and against which of the defendants. as such there being full compliance of such rule in the judgment of the trial court, the appellate court rightly passed the impugned judgment dismissing the appeal. He then submits that the suit was filed on 12.5.1985 challenging the decision taken by the defendants No. 1 to 4 on 4.5.1985. Thereafter in about 14 years i.e. till 1999 several changes have been brought by the school authority which compelled the plaintiff to amend his plaint in accordance with the requirements and as such the suit was not filed challenging the suspension order dated 13.5.1985 of the plaintiff. Rather that is one of the amendments brought by the plaintiff in the prayer portion as he was suspended on the very next day of institution of the suit Similarly other prayers were also made as and when the school authority and the members of the Managing Committee took different decisions as regards his service. Thus the submissions of Mr. Shahid Ahmed as to filing of the suit before the suspension order was passed is not sustainable in law. Mr. Amin lastly submits that the judgment of the lower appellate court is a proper judgment of affirmance. The appellant petitioner did not raise any of these questions before the appellate court which has been raised here, rather the point raised before the Court of appeal below was simply that the defendant had no knowledge of the suit he was not aware of the date and as such the ex-parte decree passed being beyond his knowledge is liable to be set aside. In this regard Mr. Amin submits that the appellant added as defendant No. 21 by amending the plaint when he was given the charge of the office of the Head Master and he entered appearance in the suit on 25.5.1999 and after taking several adjournments he filed written objection against the application for temporary injunction and thereafter he took several adjournments from time to time in the suit which proves that he had full knowledge of the suit and accordingly the learned Additional District Judge rightly held that the defendant appellants lack of knowledge of the suit being the only point raised by the appellant has been found to be not believable., Mr. Amin relying on an Indian decision reported in AIR 1964 (ORISSA) 98 submits that in an ex-parte case, Judgments are cryptic, evidence is barely referred to and hardly elaborate discussions are made. Mrs Mrely from the fact of absence of elaborate discussion, as in contested cases, it cannot be said that the court did not apply its judicial mind and did not appreciate the issue and evidence, properly. Thus he submits that the impugned judgment does not suffer from any error of law wherein this court's interference under the revisional jurisdiction can be called for.
